prompt: What does "benevolent" mean? "The benevolent queen gave bread to every family."

prompt: What does "scarce" mean? "Fresh water was scarce in the dry valley."

subject: reading
prompt: What does "frugal" mean? "A frugal family reuses jars instead of throwing them away."

subject: reading

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: Bees visit flowers to drink nectar. As they move from flower to flower, pollen sticks to their legs. This pollen helps new seeds and fruits to grow.
choices: Bees help plants make seeds and fruit.
Flowers are all the same color.
Bees live in very cold places.
answer: Bees help plants make seeds and fruit.
hint: Look at what the pollen helps grow.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: Maria wanted to learn the guitar. At first her fingers hurt and the notes sounded wrong. She practiced each day, and soon she could play a whole song.
choices: Practice helps you get better at something.
answer: Practice helps you get better at something.
hint: Think about what changed because she practiced each day.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: The moon has no air and no wind. Because of this, the footprints left there long ago have not changed. They may stay for millions of years.
choices: Footprints are easy to wash away.
Footprints on the moon last a very long time.
People visit the moon every day.
answer: Footprints on the moon last a very long time.
hint: Ask why the footprints have not changed.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: A library is more than a place for books. Many libraries lend games, tools, and music. Some also hold classes and story hours for all ages.
choices: Story hours are only for adults.
Libraries offer many things besides books.
answer: Libraries offer many things besides books.
hint: The passage lists several things libraries share.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: Long ago, people sent messages by horse. Later, the telegraph sent words along wires in minutes. Today, a message can reach a friend in a blink.
choices: Sending messages has become faster over time.
answer: Sending messages has become faster over time.
hint: Follow how the time to send a message changes.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: Ants work together to build their homes. Some dig tunnels, some carry food, and some care for the young. Each ant has a job that helps the whole group.
choices: Ants share the work to help their group.
answer: Ants share the work to help their group.
hint: Notice that every ant has a job.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: Sleep gives your body time to rest and grow. It also helps your brain hold on to what you learned that day. Kids who sleep well often do better at school.
choices: Good sleep helps your body and your learning.
answer: Good sleep helps your body and your learning.
hint: Think about what sleep does for body and brain.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: A tiny seed holds a plan for a whole tree. With water, sunlight, and time, it sends roots down and a stem up. Years later, it may be taller than a house.
choices: Roots grow up toward the sky.
Small seeds can grow into very big trees.
answer: Small seeds can grow into very big trees.
hint: Compare the size of the seed with the size of the tree.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: Rivers carve paths through rock over many years. Water moves bits of stone and sand a little at a time. After a very long time, a deep canyon can form.
choices: Moving water can slowly shape the land.
answer: Moving water can slowly shape the land.
hint: The key words are water and a very long time.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: Tomas forgot his lunch at home. His friend Jada shared half of her sandwich without being asked. Tomas smiled and thanked her, and the next day he brought extra snacks to share.
choices: Lunch should be left at home.
Kindness can spread from one friend to another.
answer: Kindness can spread from one friend to another.
hint: See what Tomas did after Jada was kind.

subject: reading
prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
passage: Many birds fly south when the weather turns cold. They travel to places where food is easier to find. When spring comes, they fly back home.
choices: All birds stay in one place.
Some birds travel to find food and warm weather.
answer: Some birds travel to find food and warm weather.
hint: Ask why the birds leave and why they return.
